ngvb: latent non-Gaussian models with R-INLA

Source: vignettes/ngvb_pkg.Rmd
ngvb_pkg.Rmd

ngvb takes an ordinary R-INLA latent Gaussian model (LGM), checks whether the latent Gaussian assumption is adequate, and extends it to a latent non-Gaussian model (LnGM), each in one line:

LGM <- inla(y ~ f(s, model = "rw1"), data = d, control.compute = list(config = TRUE))

ng.check(LGM)       # is the latent Gaussian assumption adequate, and where not?
LnGM <- ngvb(LGM)   # fit the non-Gaussian extension

Every worked example in the documentation needs INLA, which is not distributed on CRAN. The vignettes are therefore hosted on the package website rather than shipped with the package, so that they always build against a working INLA installation. They are listed below.

Vignettes

  • Get started with ngvb — what a latent non-Gaussian model is, which INLA components are supported, and a first end-to-end example on a time series with two jumps.
  • Geostatistical data: a Matern (SPDE) field — a Matern field fitted to pressure readings, with a map of where the spatial predictions will move before the non-Gaussian model is ever fitted.
  • Areal data: an intrinsic model (besag) — an intrinsic conditional autoregression for burglary rates across Columbus, Ohio.
  • Random intercepts and slopes — subject-level random effects in a longitudinal growth study.
  • Custom models: your own precision matrix — building a simultaneous autoregression by hand with ngvb_custom(), and borrowing ready-made operators from the ngme2 package.

The full function reference is at https://rafaelcabral-ai.github.io/ngvb/reference/index.html.

Installing INLA 

install.packages("INLA",
  repos = c(getOption("repos"), INLA = "https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"),
  dep = TRUE)

References

  • Cabral, R., Bolin, D. and Rue, H. (2024). Fitting latent non-Gaussian models using variational Bayes and Laplace approximations. Journal of the American Statistical Association 119(548):2983–2995. https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.2023.2296704
  • Cabral, R., Bolin, D. and Rue, H. (2025). Robustness, model checking, and hierarchical models. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B 87(3):632–652. https://doi.org/10.1093/jrsssb/qkae107
